plan.english: Boy, listen to my words. When it grows bright, stand up and yoke the two oxen. Put the yoke on their shoulders. Then lead the team into the field. The two draw the plough, and you keep it straight. Do not strike them; speak to them. An ox that you strike quickly grows tired. When the sun stands above, give the thirsty pair water. He who guards his own team eats grain.

clauses.english: Boy, listen to my words.
When it grows bright, stand up and yoke the two oxen.
Put the yoke on their shoulders.
Then lead the team into the field.
The two draw the plough, and you keep it straight.
Do not strike them; speak to them.
An ox that you strike quickly grows tired.
When the sun stands above, give the thirsty pair water.
He who guards his own team eats grain.

plan.english: Son, listen; I have seen many winters. When the earth thaws, then plough. Do not plough a field that is dry. In dry earth the plough breaks, and the team sweats. Draw the plough through the whole field three times. Then the seed lies in it and grows. Ploughed land is fruitful and gives much grain. When you grasp the plough, do not turn around; look forward. Remember these words, son.

clauses.english: Son, listen; I have seen many winters.
When the earth thaws, then plough.
Do not plough a field that is dry.
In dry earth the plough breaks, and the team sweats.
Draw the plough through the whole field three times.
Then the seed lies in it and grows.
Ploughed land is fruitful and gives much grain.
When you grasp the plough, do not turn around; look forward.
Remember these words, son.

plan.english: Carry the seed to the ploughed land early. Walk through it and cast the seed. Cover it. If the seed lies on it, the wild beasts and the worms devour it. When it has rained, sow. Water nourishes the seed, and the sun ripens the grain. As many seeds as you sow, so many ears grow. Do not cast seed with an angry heart. Then drive the cattle away.

clauses.english: Carry the seed to the ploughed land early.
Walk through it and cast the seed.
Cover it.
If the seed lies on it, the wild beasts and the worms devour it.
When it has rained, sow.
Water nourishes the seed, and the sun ripens the grain.
As many seeds as you sow, so many ears grow.
Do not cast seed with an angry heart.
Then drive the cattle away.

plan.english: Daughter, rise early; the night is leaving. Go to the hearth and look at the fire. If the fire has gone out, bring dry twigs. Lay them on it and give the fire breath. Then it grows strong; it licks the twigs and burns. Fire warms the house and drives away the night. Guard the fire through the night. A fireless house grows cold.

clauses.english: Daughter, rise early; the night is leaving.
Go to the hearth and look at the fire.
If the fire has gone out, bring dry twigs.
Lay them on it and give the fire breath.
Then it grows strong; it licks the twigs and burns.
Fire warms the house and drives away the night.
Guard the fire through the night.
A fireless house grows cold.

plan.english: Daughter, bring water inside. Put the grain in it and set it on the fire. When it boils, the grain cooks. If it burns, your father grows angry. Do not leave the hearth; sit and watch. When it has become tasty, give it to the men. They come hungry and thirsty from the field. He who has eaten, he works.

clauses.english: Daughter, bring water inside.
Put the grain in it and set it on the fire.
When it boils, the grain cooks.
If it burns, your father grows angry.
Do not leave the hearth; sit and watch.
When it has become tasty, give it to the men.
They come hungry and thirsty from the field.
He who has eaten, he works.

plan.english: Dawn shone, and Man-Minded woke. He yoked the two oxen and led them to the field. His son carried the seed about. The team drew the plough through the earth. Man-Minded ploughed, and the son sowed. When the sun was above, they sat down under an oak. They ate wheat and drank. Then they worked again. When it grew dark, the two went off.

clauses.english: Dawn shone, and Man-Minded woke.
He yoked the two oxen and led them to the field.
His son carried the seed about.
The team drew the plough through the earth.
Man-Minded ploughed, and the son sowed.
When the sun was above, they sat down under an oak.
They ate wheat and drank.
Then they worked again.
When it grew dark, the two went off.

plan.english: The field was dry, and the seed did not grow. The cattle were thirsty, and the dogs lay down. Good-Fame, the master of the house, looked at the sky and spoke: "Father Sky, give us water!" In the night it rained. Early the earth grew moist, and the seed grew. The cattle and the dogs drank. Good-Fame rejoiced and praised Father Sky.

clauses.english: The field was dry, and the seed did not grow.
The cattle were thirsty, and the dogs lay down.
Good-Fame, the master of the house, looked at the sky and spoke:
"Father Sky, give us water!"
In the night it rained.
Early the earth grew moist, and the seed grew.
The cattle and the dogs drank.
Good-Fame rejoiced and praised Father Sky.

plan.english: Daughter, winter is coming. Carry the wool inside and keep it safe from the worms. Your brother is bringing branches from the oaks. Lay them by the hearth; the fire dries them. When it grows cold, clothe yourself in wool. Cover the shelter of the cattle with pine branches. Lead the foal into the shelter; in winter the wolf seizes foals. The wolf does not enter a house in which the fire burns.

clauses.english: Daughter, winter is coming.
Carry the wool inside and keep it safe from the worms.
Your brother is bringing branches from the oaks.
Lay them by the hearth; the fire dries them.
When it grows cold, clothe yourself in wool.
Cover the shelter of the cattle with pine branches.
Lead the foal into the shelter; in winter the wolf seizes foals.
The wolf does not enter a house in which the fire burns.

plan.english: Hear me, friend: do not eat up the whole. Set aside the good grain for seed. Hide it from the worms. He who eats the seed, he does not sow. Seed is gold to the household. Remember this, and may your children live.

clauses.english: Hear me, friend: do not eat up the whole.
Set aside the good grain for seed.
Hide it from the worms.
He who eats the seed, he does not sow.
Seed is gold to the household.
Remember this, and may your children live.

plan.english: The sun ripened the wheat in the field. The ears swelled. Early the men went out. They cut them off and brought them inside. The wives dried the grain. They sang. The men sweated, and the daughters brought them water. When it grew dark, the master gave them their wage. Then they ate and were sated.

clauses.english: The sun ripened the wheat in the field.
The ears swelled.
Early the men went out.
They cut them off and brought them inside.
The wives dried the grain.
They sang.
The men sweated, and the daughters brought them water.
When it grew dark, the master gave them their wage.
Then they ate and were sated.

plan.english: Listen, boy: I am the cook here. At dawn prepare the hearth. I set the wheat on the fire and heat it. The fire cooks; the cook stays awake. The cook who is not awake, he burns it. Is it sour? If it is sour, it is not good. When it has become tasty, bring it to the master. When he is sated, then eat.

clauses.english: Listen, boy: I am the cook here.
At dawn prepare the hearth.
I set the wheat on the fire and heat it.
The fire cooks; the cook stays awake.
The cook who is not awake, he burns it.
Is it sour?
If it is sour, it is not good.
When it has become tasty, bring it to the master.
When he is sated, then eat.

plan.english: Daughter, the cows are lowing. Go out and milk them. Sing to them, and they stand still. The one that trembles with fear gives nothing. Then drive them to the pasture, and the dog guards them. When it grows dark, the wolf comes. Then lead the cows back to the shelter. In the shelter the foal follows its mother.

clauses.english: Daughter, the cows are lowing.
Go out and milk them.
Sing to them, and they stand still.
The one that trembles with fear gives nothing.
Then drive them to the pasture, and the dog guards them.
When it grows dark, the wolf comes.
Then lead the cows back to the shelter.
In the shelter the foal follows its mother.

title: The ox that would not rise

plan.english: The ox lay in the field and did not rise. The boy struck it, and it did not stand. Then Kindly came. He said: "Do not strike it. It is thirsty." The boy gave it water, and it drank. Then it stood up and drew the plough. Kindly said: "A team that is thirsty does not work. Love your team, and it loves you." And the boy learned.

clauses.english: The ox lay in the field and did not rise.
The boy struck it, and it did not stand.
Then Kindly came.
He said: "Do not strike it.
It is thirsty."
The boy gave it water, and it drank.
Then it stood up and drew the plough.
Kindly said: "A team that is thirsty does not work.
Love your team, and it loves you."
And the boy learned.

plan.english: The wheel of the sun turns, and our work turns with it. When the earth thaws, plough. When it grows warm, sow. When the grain has ripened, cut off the ears. When winter comes, sit down at the hearth and eat. Then straighten the plough and guard the seed. This is the work of a free man.

clauses.english: The wheel of the sun turns, and our work turns with it.
When the earth thaws, plough.
When it grows warm, sow.
When the grain has ripened, cut off the ears.
When winter comes, sit down at the hearth and eat.
Then straighten the plough and guard the seed.
This is the work of a free man.

plan.english: When it was growing dark, a guest came to the house. The mistress led him to the hearth. She said: "Dear guest, sit down and be well." Her daughter gave him grain. The guest ate and was satisfied. He praised the mistress: "May the gods give you good things. I am Of-Divine-Race." At dawn he went away.

clauses.english: When it was growing dark, a guest came to the house.
The mistress led him to the hearth.
She said: "Dear guest, sit down and be well."
Her daughter gave him grain.
The guest ate and was satisfied.
He praised the mistress:
"May the gods give you good things.
I am Of-Divine-Race."
At dawn he went away.

plan.english: Make the plough out of oak. The pine breaks; the oak stands. Split it and make it straight. Join the plough and the yoke. If the plough breaks in the field, the work lies still. So look at your plough at night and at dawn. Lift the plough onto the shoulder and carry it out.

clauses.english: Make the plough out of oak.
The pine breaks; the oak stands.
Split it and make it straight.
Join the plough and the yoke.
If the plough breaks in the field, the work lies still.
So look at your plough at night and at dawn.
Lift the plough onto the shoulder and carry it out.

plan.english: Of-Divine-Race, when you cook grain, give some to Agni. Agni is the giver of good things. He warms us and feeds us. Speak to him with dear words: "Agni, guard this hearth, and may you be kindly to us." My mother told me these things.

clauses.english: Of-Divine-Race, when you cook grain, give some to Agni.
Agni is the giver of good things.
He warms us and feeds us.
Speak to him with dear words:
"Agni, guard this hearth, and may you be kindly to us."
My mother told me these things.

plan.english: It grew dark, and the sheep lay in the pasture. The shepherd sat by the fire and stayed awake. Above, the stars shone. A wolf crept toward the sheep. The dog heard it and cried out. The shepherd stood up, seized a burning branch, and drove it away. It grew afraid and fled. And the shepherd guarded the sheep through the night.

clauses.english: It grew dark, and the sheep lay in the pasture.
The shepherd sat by the fire and stayed awake.
Above, the stars shone.
A wolf crept toward the sheep.
The dog heard it and cried out.
The shepherd stood up, seized a burning branch, and drove it away.
It grew afraid and fled.
And the shepherd guarded the sheep through the night.

plan.english: When the men bring the ears in, lay them in the sun, and it dries them. If it rains, take them to the shelter. Why do we dry them? Grain that grows moist becomes sour. Then put them inside. So in winter there is grain, and the children are not hungry.

clauses.english: When the men bring the ears in, lay them in the sun, and it dries them.
If it rains, take them to the shelter.
Why do we dry them?
Grain that grows moist becomes sour.
Then put them inside.
So in winter there is grain, and the children are not hungry.

plan.english: There was a servant who did not love work. When the master ploughed, the idle one lay under the oak. When he cut the ears, the idle one lay still. Winter came. Grain lay in his house. The idle one was hungry. He came to the master and sought something. The master said: "He who does not plough, he is hungry."

clauses.english: There was a servant who did not love work.
When the master ploughed, the idle one lay under the oak.
When he cut the ears, the idle one lay still.
Winter came.
Grain lay in his house.
The idle one was hungry.
He came to the master and sought something.
The master said: "He who does not plough, he is hungry."

plan.english: Son of my brother, look at the sky. If the sky is red, it will rain; do not cast seed. When the wind roars, Perkwunos is coming. Then the sheep tremble, and the horses grow restless. Drive the sheep and the foals together. When the stars shine at night, it will grow bright early. Your father knows these things; now you too know them. He who knows the wind does not go astray.

clauses.english: Son of my brother, look at the sky.
If the sky is red, it will rain; do not cast seed.
When the wind roars, Perkwunos is coming.
Then the sheep tremble, and the horses grow restless.
Drive the sheep and the foals together.
When the stars shine at night, it will grow bright early.
Your father knows these things; now you too know them.
He who knows the wind does not go astray.

plan.english: Night has come, and the fire burns. The mother lays the children down by it. She covers them with wool and sings: "Lie down, children; the dog guards you. Your father has come back; the horses are standing still. The grain lies inside; no one is hungry. The wolf is yonder." So she sang, and she put them to sleep.

clauses.english: Night has come, and the fire burns.
The mother lays the children down by it.
She covers them with wool and sings:
"Lie down, children; the dog guards you.
Your father has come back; the horses are standing still.
The grain lies inside; no one is hungry.
The wolf is yonder."
So she sang, and she put them to sleep.

plan.english: Of-Goodly-Fame took a seed and showed it to his son, Good-Horses. "What is in this seed?" said Good-Horses. Of-Goodly-Fame said: "Wheat and many seeds are in it. Hide it in the earth; then you will see." Good-Horses put the seed into the ploughed land. The seed came forth and grew. Good-Horses saw it and was astonished. His father said: "So the seed becomes grain, and the grain becomes seed."

clauses.english: Of-Goodly-Fame took a seed and showed it to his son, Good-Horses.
"What is in this seed?" said Good-Horses.
Of-Goodly-Fame said: "Wheat and many seeds are in it.
Hide it in the earth; then you will see."
Good-Horses put the seed into the ploughed land.
The seed came forth and grew.
Good-Horses saw it and was astonished.
His father said: "So the seed becomes grain, and the grain becomes seed."

plan.english: Friend, you work for me; I give you a wage. I owe you the wage; you owe me the work. Wake at dawn and go out with the team. Do not lean on the plough; work. When it grows dark, come back. Then sit and drink. He who works receives a good wage. He who steals from me, him I drive away.

clauses.english: Friend, you work for me; I give you a wage.
I owe you the wage; you owe me the work.
Wake at dawn and go out with the team.
Do not lean on the plough; work.
When it grows dark, come back.
Then sit and drink.
He who works receives a good wage.
He who steals from me, him I drive away.

plan.english: Good-Horses, the mistress, awoke and spoke to the servants: "You, stretch out the wool. You, split branches for the fire. And you, drive the sheep to the pasture. You, make the wagon ready. I cook." They went out and did the work. When they arrived, Good-Horses gave them grain.

clauses.english: Good-Horses, the mistress, awoke and spoke to the servants:
"You, stretch out the wool.
You, split branches for the fire.
And you, drive the sheep to the pasture.
You, make the wagon ready.
I cook."
They went out and did the work.
When they arrived, Good-Horses gave them grain.

plan.english: When it grew bright, the man went out. He yoked the oxen and spoke: "Mother Earth, receive the seed and nourish it. Give us much grain, and we will praise you." The plough split the field, and the seed fell into it. His wife sang.

clauses.english: When it grew bright, the man went out.
He yoked the oxen and spoke:
"Mother Earth, receive the seed and nourish it.
Give us much grain, and we will praise you."
The plough split the field, and the seed fell into it.
His wife sang.

plan.english: Of-Divine-Race, hear these words about the fire. Do not throw water on the fire. Do not urinate toward the fire or toward the sun. Agni is a god. He sees our deeds. Feed him with dry pine, and he will protect you. At night cover the fire; at dawn it wakes.

clauses.english: Of-Divine-Race, hear these words about the fire.
Do not throw water on the fire.
Do not urinate toward the fire or toward the sun.
Agni is a god.
He sees our deeds.
Feed him with dry pine, and he will protect you.
At night cover the fire; at dawn it wakes.

plan.english: The father was at work in the field. The mother heated grain and said to the two children: "Carry this to him; he is hungry." The two went off. He saw them and rejoiced. He ate, and the two sat near him. Then he worked again, and the two children sang.

clauses.english: The father was at work in the field.
The mother heated grain and said to the two children:
"Carry this to him; he is hungry."
The two went off.
He saw them and rejoiced.
He ate, and the two sat near him.
Then he worked again, and the two children sang.

plan.english: Friend, the seed is the father of the grain. Ploughed land is its mother. The sky warms it and feeds it. And the man who ploughs is the shepherd of the field. Guard the seed and the field. He who knows this grows rich. And may your house be filled with grain.

clauses.english: Friend, the seed is the father of the grain.
Ploughed land is its mother.
The sky warms it and feeds it.
And the man who ploughs is the shepherd of the field.
Guard the seed and the field.
He who knows this grows rich.
And may your house be filled with grain.

plan.english: The men went to the pines and cut them down. They laid them there. When they had dried out, they burned them. The fire burned, and the wild beasts fled. A snake crept out of the fire. Then they drew the plough through that field and cast wheat. It grew rich in grain.

clauses.english: The men went to the pines and cut them down.
They laid them there.
When they had dried out, they burned them.
The fire burned, and the wild beasts fled.
A snake crept out of the fire.
Then they drew the plough through that field and cast wheat.
It grew rich in grain.

plan.english: When a guest arrives, lead him to the fire. Seat him by the fire and give him grain. When he has eaten, then he will tell his name. The guest is dear to the gods. Whoever drives a guest away, the gods strike him down. Lay wool for him, and let him lie down. When he goes away, give him gold.

clauses.english: When a guest arrives, lead him to the fire.
Seat him by the fire and give him grain.
When he has eaten, then he will tell his name.
The guest is dear to the gods.
Whoever drives a guest away, the gods strike him down.
Lay wool for him, and let him lie down.
When he goes away, give him gold.

plan.english: Set names on your team. One that knows its name listens to you. When you yoke them, speak their names. When they arrive at the oak, lead them back. Do not rage at them. Sing to them, and they pull the plough.

clauses.english: Set names on your team.
One that knows its name listens to you.
When you yoke them, speak their names.
When they arrive at the oak, lead them back.
Do not rage at them.
Sing to them, and they pull the plough.

plan.english: The men accomplished their work. The wagons carried the ears to the shelter. Good-Horses, the mistress, filled the shelter with wheat. The cook prepared it, and they ate. They drank and sang and praised the gods: "Gods, givers of good things, give us grain again!" The guests praised the cook.

clauses.english: The men accomplished their work.
The wagons carried the ears to the shelter.
Good-Horses, the mistress, filled the shelter with wheat.
The cook prepared it, and they ate.
They drank and sang and praised the gods:
"Gods, givers of good things, give us grain again!"
The guests praised the cook.

plan.english: Daughter, when you go to your husband, cherish his mother. Love his sister and his brother. Guard his fire. Rise early and do the work. A wife who is wakeful fills the house with good things. And her name is famous. Remember these words.

clauses.english: Daughter, when you go to your husband, cherish his mother.
Love his sister and his brother.
Guard his fire.
Rise early and do the work.
A wife who is wakeful fills the house with good things.
And her name is famous.
Remember these words.

plan.english: Perkwunos roared above. The horses trembled and the foals lay down. The wind broke the ears of grain. Of-Goodly-Fame went out and saw the field. He grew afraid; the grain was lost. Then his wife said: "Do not be afraid. We have wheat inside. We will sow again, and the grain will grow."

clauses.english: Perkwunos roared above.
The horses trembled and the foals lay down.
The wind broke the ears of grain.
Of-Goodly-Fame went out and saw the field.
He grew afraid; the grain was lost.
Then his wife said: "Do not be afraid.
We have wheat inside.
We will sow again, and the grain will grow."

plan.english: Friend, the dog is your brother in the pasture. Feed him. When you lie down, he guards the sheep. He hears well; he hears at night. When the wolf comes, he cries out. Do not strike him; do not drive him from the fire. If he is gone, the wolf devours them.

clauses.english: Friend, the dog is your brother in the pasture.
Feed him.
When you lie down, he guards the sheep.
He hears well; he hears at night.
When the wolf comes, he cries out.
Do not strike him; do not drive him from the fire.
If he is gone, the wolf devours them.

title: Brother and sister at the hearth

plan.english: "Brother, the fire is not burning; bring branches." "Where are they?" "They lie by the shelter." The brother brought them and laid them on the fire. The fire grew strong, and the sister heated grain. "Are you hungry, brother?" "I am hungry." "Then sit down and eat." And the two sat down by the fire and ate up the grain.

clauses.english: "Brother, the fire is not burning; bring branches."
"Where are they?"
"They lie by the shelter."
The brother brought them and laid them on the fire.
The fire grew strong, and the sister heated grain.
"Are you hungry, brother?"
"I am hungry."
"Then sit down and eat."
And the two sat down by the fire and ate up the grain.

plan.english: Do not yoke horses to the plough. The horse is swift; it runs and it tires. The ox does not run, and it does not tire. Yoke the horses to the chariot, the oxen to the plough. The warrior drives horses on; the master of the house drives the plough. The ox toils; the horse eats. Do your own work.

clauses.english: Do not yoke horses to the plough.
The horse is swift; it runs and it tires.
The ox does not run, and it does not tire.
Yoke the horses to the chariot, the oxen to the plough.
The warrior drives horses on; the master of the house drives the plough.
The ox toils; the horse eats.
Do your own work.

plan.english: Fame-from-the-Gods did the work in the king's field. He drew the plough, he cast the seed, he cut off the ears. When the grain was inside, the king gave him a wage, a measure of wheat. Fame-from-the-Gods brought it to his own mother. She saw him and rejoiced. She said: "My son, you have done good work. May your fame be imperishable."

clauses.english: Fame-from-the-Gods did the work in the king's field.
He drew the plough, he cast the seed, he cut off the ears.
When the grain was inside, the king gave him a wage, a measure of wheat.
Fame-from-the-Gods brought it to his own mother.
She saw him and rejoiced.
She said: "My son, you have done good work.
May your fame be imperishable."

plan.english: Hear these words. The field feeds the man; the man works it. The plough tears the earth; the seed fills it. From work comes grain, and by it we live. He who lies down at dawn sees nothing in winter. The gods give, and the man toils. May the gods give you much grain and great fame.

clauses.english: Hear these words.
The field feeds the man; the man works it.
The plough tears the earth; the seed fills it.
From work comes grain, and by it we live.
He who lies down at dawn sees nothing in winter.
The gods give, and the man toils.
May the gods give you much grain and great fame.
